_comment: Modules are the between-acts choice: after winning an act that continues a chain, three of these are offered and one is kept for the rest of the board. They reset when the campaign moves to a new board, because a board is a contract and a run that could accumulate every module across forty-eight levels would end as a single obvious stack rather than as a series of decisions. Each one deliberately touches a DIFFERENT system - rate, damage, reach, refunds, interest, opening Capital, integrity, the support-link radius, jam resistance - so a draft is a question about what this board actually needs rather than a comparison of three numbers on the same axis. Effects are modest on purpose: three or four of them across a chain should feel like a build, not like a difficulty setting. Anything that reads as strictly-best in every draft has failed and should be re-tuned rather than removed, because a module nobody ever picks is dead content and a module everybody picks is not a choice.
